content.title: About
content.content: Cashews are the edible seeds of the cashew tree (Anacardium occidentale), native to tropical regions of Africa and South America. The nuts have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a buttery texture. Cashews are eaten raw, roasted, salted, or as a paste, and are used in sauces, desserts, and vegan dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cashew grows on a tree that produces a fruit (the cashew apple) and the nut hangs from the bottom of the fruit in a shell.
The seed is covered by a soft skin that is usually removed before consumption.
Only the fully ripened fruit is safe to eat; the raw shell contains urushiol, a toxic compound removed during processing.
Cashews are commonly used to make cashew oil, cashew butter, and vegan cheese alternatives.
A mature cashew tree can reach up to 12 meters tall and remain productive for up to 30 years.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: Cashews contain primarily monounsaturated fatty acids, which support heart health.

items.title: Source of magnesium
items.content: Magnesium in cashews helps maintain normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Contains copper and iron
items.content: Cashews provide copper and iron, essential for hemoglobin formation and energy metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The nuts are a good source of B1, B6, and folate, supporting metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Protein and fiber
items.content: Cashews supply plant protein and dietary fiber, promoting satiety and digestive health.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Cashews can trigger allergic reactions, potentially severe, in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Cashews are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Raw toxicity
items.content: Raw cashews contain urushiol, a toxic resin; therefore, commercial cashews are always heat‑treated.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Whole cashews can pose a choking risk for young children; finely chopped or ground nuts are recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cashews can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, oatmeal, yogurt, baked goods, or blended into cashew butter. They are also used in sauces, curries, and vegan cheese recipes. Soaking them for a few hours softens the texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cashews in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent oil oxidation. Discard nuts that smell rancid or stale.
